subject: Renewal structure: phased ramp + co-terming options for Brightwell
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@brightwell.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightwell.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal / term structure questions and co-terming request

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the renewal kickoff yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with explicit asks so they can make a recommendation internally. High level: Brightwell is looking to convert our current 12‑month commitment into a multi‑year arrangement that lines up with our product contract (co‑term). Key constraints from procurement:

- We need the new Redwood term to co‑term with our product license (expires 2029‑02‑28).
- We prefer a 24‑month window, but are open to 36 months if we can get a predictable ramp schedule and a midterm true‑up.
- Procurement will not accept unconditional auto‑renew; they want an opt‑out/notice window (60 days) and a renewal review.
- We want the ability to add burst capacity in Q1 of each year with pre‑defined pricing bands.

Can you propose 2–3 concrete term structures (one short: 24m phased ramp, one long: 36m with smoothing credits, and one hybrid with frontloaded credits + quarterly true‑ups)? Also need an MAP (mutual action plan) with dates — procurement needs approvals by April 12 so we can get legal and finance onboarded.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Cloud Ops, Brightwell AI

--
Attachment: procurement_requirements_2028.pdf (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightwell.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal / term structure questions and co-terming request

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. I put together three playbook options (high‑level) and attached a short PDF with modeling: Renewal_Options_v1.pdf. TL;DR:

Option A — 24m phased ramp (preferred by client)
- Term: 24 months, co‑term to 2029‑02‑28
- Ramp: 50% committed capacity months 1–4, 75% months 5–8, 100% month 9 onward
- Billing: quarterly in arrears; true‑up at month 12 and month 24
- Auto‑renew: disabled; manual renewal with 60‑day notice

Option B — 36m smoothing (discounted forward commitment)
- Term: 36 months co‑term aligned to nearest fiscal quarter
- Ramp: smoothing credits frontloaded to offset early months; quarterly true‑ups
- Billing: annual prepay or quarterly with committed minimums
- Auto‑renew: opt‑in only with explicit exec approval

Option C — Hybrid frontload + burst lanes
- 24m base with optional 12m extension trigger if usage>120% of committed
- Burst pool defined with fixed pricing bands and reserve credits for first two bursts

Vanessa/Jordan — can you validate whether Option A pricing and the proposed billing cadence are acceptable from revenue recognition and AR perspective? If so I’ll push the MAP and a DocuSign placeholder to Elena’s team.

Elena — if you can confirm whether procurement prefers quarterly true‑ups vs. annual, I will finalize the MAP.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Renewal_Options_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal / term structure questions and co-terming request

Quick finance ops note after reviewing Renewal_Options_v1: we can support Option A (24m phased ramp) but suggest the following tweaks to keep AR / rev rec predictable:

- Billing cadence: quarterly in arrears is fine, but add month‑end true‑ups for usage variance so revenue buckets are accurate for ERP posting.
- Billing credit: provide a one‑time onboarding credit (applied month 2) to smooth customer sticker shock — model as contra‑revenue over 3 months.
- Burst lanes: reserve a small prepaid burst pool for the first 12 months that converts to paid usage if used; this avoids surprise overages.

I attached a short Billing_Ops_Summary.xlsx with the revised cashflow shape. If legal wants to allow a 36m opt‑in later, finance prefers an annual true‑up not quarterly to limit churn in recognition.

Vanessa
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Billing_Ops_Summary.xlsx (stub)

Thanks Karthik and Vanessa — that framing is helpful. Procurement prefers quarterly true‑ups (they want tighter controls), so Option A with quarterly true‑ups + the onboarding credit is our current preference. A couple more asks before I route to legal:

- Can you confirm SOC2 evidence and data retention controls will be out for legal review within three business days of the MAP?
- We need an explicit price schedule for burst lanes (two tiers) included in the DocuSign package; procurement will not sign without that.
- Decision timeline: procurement will escalate if we don’t have final commercial terms by April 12.

If you can get SOC2 artifacts and a MAP with the burst price schedule over, I’ll push to legal and our CFO.

Elena
